calls.headline: Bills draw EGP 282bn of bids as the pound firms against a 5.1% US yield
calls.body: The central bank sold EGP 114.03bn of 182- and 364-day bills on Thursday against a EGP 100bn target, from bids of EGP 282.19bn: the six-month bill yielded 26.07% and the one-year 25.02% (Egypt Telegraph, central bank). The central bank's dollar rate eased to EGP 53.50 from 53.62, a 0.2% gain for the pound, on the day the US 10-year Treasury yield rose about 12 basis points to 5.10% and the dollar index reached 103.18, a new 19-month high (Treasury, Reuters via AsiaOne). Fed funds futures now price a December hike as all but certain (CME FedWatch via CNBC).
calls.view: Demand at 2.8 times the amount sold, with yields steady near 25–26%, says the carry trade is holding even as US rates rise: foreign money is still being paid about 12 points over 12.7% inflation. That keeps the pound firm into the IMF program's December expiry and keeps local rate cuts off the table; the desk keeps the dollar in EGP 52–55.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 (central bank sell rate) before December 9.

calls.headline: EGX30 slips 0.9% as blue chips fall and foreigners sell EGP 108m
calls.line: Large caps gave back part of the week's gain while small caps kept rising, a sign of rotation rather than flight.
calls.body: The EGX30 fell 0.91% to 52,023.37 on Thursday, while the EGX70 EWI rose 0.43% to 18,527.43 (Amwal Al Ghad). Egyptians bought a net EGP 171.1m of shares, while foreigners sold EGP 107.8m and Arabs EGP 63.2m, on turnover of about EGP 10.1bn (Masrawy, Al Mal). Talaat Moustafa fell 2.0%, Telecom Egypt 1.5% and CIB 1.2%; Housing and Development Bank rose 5.8% after MSCI added it to its Egypt small cap index (Sada Elbalad), and Foodico jumped 17.5%. Decliners outnumbered gainers 127 to 90 (TradingView). The index still rose 2.3% on the week.
calls.view: A 0.9% dip after a 2.3% weekly gain, with locals buying, is profit-taking ahead of the weekend and a jump in US yields, not a turn: the index sits about 1.4% under its 50-day average of about 52,777. The desk's view that the index holds above 49,255 was right on its date; foreign selling for one session does not change that.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes below 50,000 before the end of November.

calls.headline: Brent jumps 3.3% to $95.82 after Trump says no Iran deal is needed
calls.line: Dearer oil raises Egypt's fuel import bill just as gas to industry is rationed.
calls.body: Brent settled 3.3% higher at $95.82 a barrel on Thursday after President Trump wrote that "We don't need a deal with Iran" (Rigzone, Bloomberg). Iran said two loaded supertankers were halted by explosions on a Hormuz route, while US crude stocks rose 4.7m barrels. Brent eased to about $95.4 on Friday morning (TradingView). Suez Canal transits for the latest week, to November 8, are the newest IMF PortWatch has.
calls.view: The jump undoes most of the week's fall but leaves Brent near $96, well under its 50-day average of about $104 and the desk's $105 line. For Egypt the cost is the fuel and LNG bill, which keeps the 33% gas cut to fertilizer plants in place; the desk keeps its oil view, judged November 20.

calls.headline: Juhayna's third-quarter profit rises 33%; stock slips 2.3%
calls.line: Record sales and steady margins, but the stock fell on the call.
calls.body: Juhayna's third-quarter revenue rose 25% to a record EGP 10bn and net profit 33% to EGP 654m, after a EGP 107m currency loss; EBITDA margin widened to 14.7% from 14.3% (earnings call, Investing.com transcript). Management expects the fourth quarter to match the first three and 2027 revenue growth close to this year's, with more price rises planned. The stock fell 2.3% to EGP 24.13.
calls.view: The call confirmed the growth is volume and price, not one-offs, which supports the desk's EGP 27–28 projection by end of January; the fall looks like selling into the news, not a change in the case. Exports fell 11%, the weak spot.
calls.wrong: Juhayna closes below EGP 22 before the end of January.

calls.headline: Huang quits Nvidia; Kress steps in and the stock falls 4.3%
calls.body: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's president, chief executive and director with immediate effect on Thursday, after reports of affairs including one with a woman US authorities suspect of spying for China; finance chief Colette Kress is interim chief while the board considers inside and outside candidates (Al Jazeera, Reuters via AsiaOne). The stock fell as much as 14.3% before closing 4.3% lower at $166.19, about 12 times expected earnings, its lowest since 2012 (Reuters via AsiaOne). AMD rose 5.9% and Broadcom 5.5%. Bernstein and Baird cut targets to $200 (CNBC). Nvidia reports on November 17, guided to about $108bn of revenue (August 8-K).
calls.view: The removal of uncertainty about whether Huang stays limited the damage: the stock recovered two-thirds of the day's fall. What remains is execution without a founder who ran about 60 direct reports, and that is tested on November 17. The desk's view that chips stay under pressure into Apple's results, judged on today's close, is on track with Nvidia at $166.19 against $204.64 at the start; the desk does not open a new bearish call on a stock with an RSI of 29 at 12 times earnings.
calls.wrong: Nvidia closes above $200 before the end of November.

calls.headline: 10-year yield hits 5.1% as a December hike looks certain
calls.line: Rates, not Nvidia, are the bigger weight on the market's multiple into December.
calls.body: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.10% on Thursday and the 2-year to 4.86% (Treasury), after a hot October CPI and a 3.3% jump in oil. Fed funds futures put the odds of a December hike near 100%, with about 13% on a half point, and Goldman Sachs added a March hike to its forecast (CNBC). Existing home sales fell 5.5% to a 3.75m annual rate, the slowest since August 2010, and jobless claims rose to 200,000 (Kitco). The dollar index rose 0.3% to 103.18.
calls.view: A 5% 10-year makes stocks at 7,600 dearer against bonds and hits housing first. The desk keeps its view that the S&P 500 holds above 7,250 into December 9, with confidence still medium: earnings are rising, but today's producer prices can push the half-point odds up.
calls.wrong: The S&P 500 closes below 7,250 before December 9.

calls.headline: Oil jumps 3.3% on Trump's Iran remark; Exxon rises 1.8%
calls.line: An energy bid offset part of the tech selling.
calls.body: Brent settled 3.3% higher at $95.82 and WTI 2.6% at $88.74 after President Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran (Rigzone, CNBC). Exxon rose 1.8% to $169.78. Gold fell about 2.8% to near $3,877 an ounce as yields rose (Kitco).
calls.view: The jump keeps oil in a $90–100 range rather than starting a new leg up: US stocks are building and Saudi output is rising. Exxon's projection to $185–195 by end of December still needs Brent above $105, so confidence stays low.

calls.headline: Microsoft's Outlook and Teams outage runs into a second day
calls.line: A reliability scare lands as Anthropic's office tools compete for the same customers.
calls.body: Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services were disrupted from Thursday into Friday; Microsoft ruled out a cyberattack and said early fixes did not work as expected (Forbes, TechRadar). Singapore's government email was among those affected (ITdaily). Microsoft rose 0.4% to $523.00 on Thursday and was lower before Friday's open (Yahoo Finance).
calls.view: Outages rarely change a software company's revenue, but a two-day failure feeds the story that hurt the stock this week, Anthropic's office tools. The desk keeps its low-confidence view that Microsoft lags the Nasdaq into Anthropic's listing.

drivers.why: Thursday's 182- and 364-day bills drew EGP 282.2bn of bids, 2.8 times the EGP 114bn sold, at 26.07% and 25.02% (Egypt Telegraph, central bank); that is about 12 points over 12.7% inflation.

drivers.name: Lost export dollars from gas cuts

view.headline: Bills and remittances keep the dollar in EGP 52–55
view.body: The pound firmed on a day US yields jumped, because the bill auction showed foreign and local demand intact: bids of 2.8 times the amount sold at 25–26%. Foreign bill buying and record remittances still outweigh a firmer dollar, so the pound has room to hold near EGP 53–54 into the IMF program's December 15 expiry. The risks are a half-point Fed hike, dearer oil and export dollars lost to gas cuts.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 9, or a bill auction clears with bids below the amount offered.
